title: Excel for clinical audit and quality improvement
why: Audits and QI projects need you to collect, clean and summarise care data and show change over time — usually in a spreadsheet first.
what_is_different: Clinical data must be de-identified, measured against a written standard, and shown over time (run charts) rather than as one-off averages. Small numbers and data protection rules matter more than fancy charts.

extra_modules.title: Data protection first
extra_modules.outcome: You can: collect only what you need and de-identify it
extra_modules.practice: Design a de-identified audit data-collection sheet

extra_modules.title: Measure against a standard
extra_modules.outcome: You can: calculate compliance with an audit standard
extra_modules.practice: Calculate compliance with a guideline for 50 cases

extra_modules.title: Run charts
extra_modules.outcome: You can: show improvement over time
extra_modules.practice: Build a run chart for a PDSA cycle

starter_project: Run a re-audit of a clinical standard: collect de-identified data, calculate compliance, build a run chart across two PDSA cycles and present a one-slide summary.
pitfalls: Identifiable patient data in shared files
Judging change from two data points
Changing the definition between audit cycles
